about_subtitle: Open Tavern — also known as RoleChat AI — is an independent, privacy-first platform for AI character roleplay. Chat with original romance and fantasy characters, with no install and no complicated setup.
about_why_body_1: Most AI chat tools either lock you into a subscription or quietly store your conversations on someone else's server. Open Tavern is built around a different idea:
about_why_body_2: your conversations stay between you and your AI provider.
about_why_body_3: You bring your own API key, so your prompts and replies pass directly from the app to the model provider you already choose and trust — Open Tavern does not sit in the middle reading or storing your chats.
about_why_body_4: We also wanted AI roleplay to be genuinely easy to start. No downloads, no command line, no complicated configuration. Open the app, pick a character, and begin.
about_byok_body_1: Open Tavern works with popular providers through a single API key (OpenRouter, OpenAI, and others). Because you connect your own account, you control the model, the cost, and the data — there is no middleman billing layer and no hidden storage of your conversations.
about_byok_body_2: It also reads standard character-card formats (SillyTavern V1/V2/V3 JSON and PNG), so the characters and cards you already love work here too.
about_who_body: Open Tavern is built and maintained by an independent developer. New characters and guides are added regularly, and the project keeps privacy and ease-of-use at its core.
about_cta: Questions, feedback, or a character you'd like to see?
wfc_subtitle: You've probably wondered where people actually get character cards from. Here's a list of websites where you can download bot cards and use them privately in Open Tavern, SillyTavern, or any compatible roleplay platform.
wfc_explanation_body_1: A character card is a file that contains everything about a character or chatbot: their name, appearance, personality, speaking style, backstory, example dialogues, and more.
wfc_explanation_body_2: Think of it as the character's passport. It's usually stored as a JSON file or embedded inside a PNG image, and it can be used to:
wfc_explanation_bullet_1: transfer a character between platforms (for example, from Character.AI to Janitor AI, RisuAI, SillyTavern, or Open Tavern);
wfc_explanation_bullet_2: save a copy if the original bot ever gets deleted;
wfc_explanation_bullet_3: share the character with others so they can roleplay with the same bot on their own setup.
wfc_explanation_body_3: In Open Tavern, you can drop a card file into the app and start chatting in seconds — no setup, no conversion. V1, V2, V3 JSON and SillyTavern PNG cards all work out of the box.
wfc_disclaimer_1: We are not responsible for the content hosted on these websites. They may contain uncensored or minimally moderated 18+ and fetish content. Browse at your own discretion.
wfc_disclaimer_2: These are general-purpose websites. Each character card is the responsibility of its creator, so please use your own judgment. This list is provided for informational purposes only and should not be taken as an endorsement of any particular content.
wfc_disclaimer_3: Please use these websites only to download cards for your personal use. We do not support reuploading or stealing other people's work, and we do not support character cards that violate basic ethical standards. As far as we know, there are currently no character card websites that are entirely SFW.
wfc_disclaimer_4: Many creators also share cards on Discord and other social media — if you have a favorite community, ask there too.
wfc_cta_body: Open Tavern reads every standard character card format — V1, V2, V3 JSON and SillyTavern PNG. Drop a file into the app and start chatting. No install, no setup.

home_faq_q1: Do I need to install anything?
home_faq_a1: No. RoleChat AI runs entirely in your browser. There is nothing to download or install — just open the page and start chatting.
home_faq_a2: Yes. Your API key and your conversations are stored locally in your browser. We do not run a server that reads your chats. You bring your own AI key, so your messages go directly between your browser and the AI provider you choose.
home_faq_q3: What is an API key and where do I get one?
home_faq_a3: An API key is a secret string that lets the app talk to an AI provider. You can get one from any OpenAI-compatible service. Paste it into Settings inside the app and you're ready.
home_faq_q4: Can I use my own character cards?
home_faq_a4: Yes. If you already have a character card (SillyTavern format), you can import it into the app. We're also building a library of original characters you can start with right away.
home_faq_a5: The app itself is free. You pay the AI provider you choose for the messages you generate, using your own key. There is no subscription and no middleman markup.
home_faq_q6: Do I need to understand model settings?
home_faq_a6: No. Sensible defaults are set for you. If you like, you can open the advanced options later — but you never have to in order to enjoy a great chat.

privacy_intro: Open Tavern (also called RoleChat AI) is a client-side tool. It runs in your browser and does not offer user accounts, a backend, or a server-side API. This page explains what little data is involved and how it is handled.
privacy_nodata_title: We do not collect your personal data
privacy_nodata_body: There is no login, no server-side database, and no analytics account tied to you. We do not ask for your name, email, or any personal information to use the tool. The only way we receive an email from you is if you choose to write to us.
privacy_local_title: Your data stays on your device
privacy_local_body: All of your conversations, characters, world books, and settings are stored locally in your browser (using the browser local storage and the Origin Private File System). This data never leaves your device through us. Clearing your browser data or site storage deletes it permanently, and we have no way to recover it.
privacy_api_body: Open Tavern does not run its own model server. When you chat, your messages are sent directly from your browser to the AI provider you configured, using the API key and endpoint you entered yourself. We do not proxy, read, or store these requests — they travel between your browser and your chosen provider.
privacy_third_body: The app loads some static resources from content delivery networks, such as styling and sanitization libraries and web fonts. If you enable browser-local inference, model files are downloaded directly to your browser from a public model CDN. These external services have their own privacy practices that we do not control.
privacy_cookies_body: We use a minimal cookie to remember your language preference. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies of our own. Your chats and settings are kept in the browser local storage, not in cookies.
privacy_ads_body: If advertising is shown, it may be provided by Google and other third-party advertising partners. These partners may use cookies and similar technologies to serve ads based on your past visits to this and other sites. You can opt out of personalized advertising at Google Ads Settings, and learn more at aboutads.info.
privacy_children_body: Open Tavern is not directed at children under the age of 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your country) and is not intended for use by them.
privacy_user_content_body: Open Tavern is a neutral tool. Any content you create, using your own AI provider and your own imagination, is generated and stored locally by you. We do not provide, host, or take responsibility for user-created content.
privacy_changes_body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. The date above reflects the latest revision. Continued use after changes means you accept the updated policy.
privacy_contact_body: Questions about privacy? Email us at

pt_desc: PureTavern keeps the classic SillyTavern interface, prompt system and extension support — but ships as a pure front-end you can host anywhere: Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages or your own device. Characters, chats, world books and keys are stored locally in your browser.

pt_feature_2_desc: Characters, chats, settings, world books and keys live in your browser's IndexedDB. Nothing is uploaded to the maintainer's servers.
pt_feature_3_desc: Keeps the Legacy UI, the prompt system, and a front-end compatibility layer that takes over SillyTavern /api requests in the browser.
pt_feature_4_desc: Tavern Helper 4.8.19 and Prompt Template 1.16 are bundled for offline import.
pt_feature_5_desc: Web ZIP, Android APK, iOS, HarmonyOS, desktop installers and a VS Code extension — pick the shell you like.

pt_faq_q1: Is PureTavern part of this site?
pt_faq_a1: No. PureTavern is an independent third-party open-source project (AGPL-3.0) maintained on GitHub. We feature it because it is a great fit for tavern users — always download from the official repository.
pt_faq_q2: How is it different from SillyTavern?
pt_faq_a2: Same classic interface and prompt system, but no Node.js backend: PureTavern runs as a pure static site with data in your browser, so you can host it for free on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages.
pt_faq_a3: Keys are stored locally in your browser and never sent to the maintainer's servers. Browser storage is not encrypted, though — only use builds you trust and be careful with third-party extensions.
pt_faq_a4: Yes — the project is open source under AGPL-3.0, and static hosting on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages is free. You bring your own AI key, which your provider may charge for.

stm_seo_title: SillyTavernMOD — Multi-User SillyTavern Fork for Site Owners
stm_seo_desc: SillyTavernMOD is a third-party SillyTavern fork (AGPL-3.0) that adds a site-operation suite: user registration, invite codes, quotas, shared character cards, a forum and an admin panel. Deploy with Node.js or Docker.
stm_tagline: A SillyTavern fork with a built-in site-operation suite
stm_desc: SillyTavernMOD extends the official SillyTavern (1.19) with a low-invasion sidecar module: user accounts, invite codes, storage quotas, a shared character-card library, a community forum and a full admin panel. If you want to run a tavern for many users — not just yourself — this fork is built for it.
stm_who_body: Built for site owners: running a tavern for a community, a class, a Discord server, or as a small service. If you only chat by yourself, plain SillyTavern or PureTavern is simpler.
stm_feature_1_desc: Based on official SillyTavern 1.19. All mod logic lives in a sidecar module (src/stc-mod) with only a few hooks in the core, and every change is tracked in MODIFICATIONS.md.
stm_feature_2_desc: Glassmorphism welcome, login and registration pages, invite-code signups and renewals with configurable durations.
stm_feature_3_desc: Per-user storage quotas, daily check-ins for extra space, and personal usage dashboards.
stm_feature_4_desc: An optional vault that encrypts provider keys on disk with its own separate password.
stm_feature_5_desc: Shared public character cards with one-click import, plus a forum with posts, comments and image uploads.
stm_feature_6_desc: System monitoring, batch user management, invite codes, announcements, email and OAuth settings, scheduled tasks and inactive-user cleanup.
stm_deploy_1_desc: The official image zhaiker/sillytavernmod:latest ships amd64 and arm64 builds, auto-built by GitHub Actions. Works with docker run or docker compose.
stm_deploy_2_desc: git clone, npm install, npm run start — Node.js 20.x/22.x on Windows, Linux or macOS. Run under PM2 to keep it alive in production.
stm_deploy_3_desc: Put nginx, OpenResty or Cloudflare in front for HTTPS, and set deployment.trustProxy so login IPs resolve correctly.
stm_security_body: A fresh install ships with Basic Auth enabled (admin/123456) — change it before exposing the site. Keep the project updated, and remember that as the operator you are responsible for your users' data and the API keys they entrust to you.
stm_cmp_best_st: Solo players who want the full ecosystem
stm_faq_q1: How is it different from SillyTavern?
stm_faq_a1: It's a community fork of the official release (currently 1.19) that adds site-operation features — accounts, invite codes, quotas, a card-sharing library, a forum and admin tools. The original stays a single-user client.
stm_faq_a2: If you want to run a tavern for a group or the public — with signups and quotas — yes. If you only roleplay by yourself, plain SillyTavern or PureTavern needs far less setup.
stm_faq_a3: It ships with Basic Auth (admin/123456) enabled by default — change the password immediately. API keys in the vault are encrypted with a separate password, but as with any public site, use HTTPS and keep updates current.
stm_faq_a4: The project is open source under AGPL-3.0. You cover your own server and AI API costs; the invite-code system can hook into your own purchase links if you want paid access.
stm_faq_q5: Can it keep up with official updates?
stm_faq_a5: Yes — the mod logic is isolated in src/stc-mod with only a few documented hooks in the core (see MODIFICATIONS.md), so the fork is designed to track official SillyTavern releases.

cs_desc: A full character-card workshop for SillyTavern V2/V3 cards: form editing for every field, AI-assisted writing, macro autocomplete, a completeness score with fix suggestions, and one-click PNG/JSON export with embedded data. Nothing is uploaded — cards live in your browser storage.
cs_feature_1_desc: Name, description, personality, scenario, greetings, example dialogues, system prompt, post-history instructions and tags — the complete V2/V3 field set with alternate greetings.
cs_feature_2_desc: One click per field: the AI drafts description, personality, scenario or an opening message from your existing content. You review and apply — nothing is written blindly.

cs_faq_a5: Exports follow the published V2/V3 character card specs, so they load in SillyTavern, compatible forks, RisuAI and the RoleChat AI app on this site. Unknown fields from imported cards are preserved on export.

cmp_tagline: Same hobby, different trade-offs — pick yours.

wb_desc: A complete workshop for SillyTavern world info (lorebooks): every entry field from keywords and insertion order to recursion, probability and depth injection, drag-and-drop ordering, batch operations, and a live match preview against sample chat text. Imports ST world info JSON, lorebook_v3 files and character-book entries — everything stays in your browser.
wb_feature_1_desc: Keywords, secondary keys, trigger logic, insertion order and position, depth and role, probability, recursion flags, group scoring, timers and automation IDs — the complete ST world info surface in one form.
wb_feature_2_desc: Grab a row's handle to rearrange entries; insertion order is renumbered automatically. Up/down buttons are there as a fallback, and every change saves instantly.
wb_feature_3_desc: Select any number of entries and enable, disable, delete, re-position or re-set probability for all of them in one click — ideal for tuning large lorebooks.

wb_feature_5_desc: Import SillyTavern world info JSON, lorebook_v3 files, or a character card's embedded book; export back to ST world info or V3 lorebook with all fields preserved.
wb_feature_6_desc: Your worldbooks never leave the browser — stored locally (OPFS + localStorage), no account, no upload, no tracking of what you write.

wb_step_2_desc: Add entries, fill in keywords and content, tune position, order, logic and advanced fields — every change is saved to your browser as you type.

wb_faq_q1: Which file formats can I import?
wb_faq_a1: SillyTavern world info JSON (entries object format), lorebook_v3 files, character_book entries arrays, and V2/V3 character cards with an embedded character_book — the format is detected automatically.
wb_faq_a2: Roughly: the total characters of all entry contents plus keywords divided by 4, which approximates English token counts. Treat it as a magnitude check against your context budget, not an exact tokenizer.
wb_faq_q3: How does the hit preview work?
wb_faq_a3: It simulates SillyTavern's activation: disabled entries are skipped, constant entries always fire, and keyword matches respect per-entry or global case sensitivity and whole-word settings. Secondary keys are combined by the entry's logic (AND_ANY, NOT_ALL, NOT_ANY, AND_ALL).
wb_faq_a4: Only in this browser (OPFS + localStorage), like the rest of the tool box. Export important worldbooks as files — clearing site data will remove them.

cc_desc: A converter workbench for roleplay character cards: drop in files from another platform, get automatic format detection and synonym field mapping, review each conversion with a completeness score, then export SillyTavern V2/V3 JSON or PNG.
cc_feature_1_desc: Recognizes SillyTavern V1/V2/V3, RisuAI, AgnAI, TextGeneration WebUI, Chub exports and plain-text persona dumps — automatically, for every file.
cc_feature_2_desc: char_persona, world_scenario, char_greeting, example_dialogue — foreign fields are matched to their SillyTavern counterparts through a curated synonym table.
cc_feature_3_desc: Fields without a SillyTavern counterpart are listed as unmapped keys on each card, so you always know exactly what converted and what needs a manual copy.
cc_feature_4_desc: Every converted card gets a 0–100 completeness score and lists its filled fields with character counts — spot thin imports at a glance.

cc_feature_6_desc: Conversion runs entirely in your browser. No account, no upload — your characters never leave this device.

cc_step_1_desc: Drag in .json or .png character cards from any platform, or paste raw JSON straight into the text box.
cc_step_2_desc: Check the detected source, filled fields and completeness score; rename the card and see which keys stayed unmapped.
cc_step_3_desc: Download V2/V3 JSON or a PNG with the card embedded, or save it into Card Studio to keep editing.

cc_faq_a1: SillyTavern V1/V2/V3 as JSON or PNG, RisuAI exports, AgnAI character JSON, TextGeneration WebUI character JSON, Chub exports with a nested card object, and plain-text persona dumps.
cc_faq_q2: What happens to fields the spec does not have?
cc_faq_a2: They are reported as unmapped keys on the conversion preview. Core fields are mapped through a synonym table; anything else is listed so you can copy it over manually if needed.

cc_faq_q4: Why does my converted card score low?

at_seo_title: AI Toolkit — Free Online AI Generators for SillyTavern Characters, Greetings, Worldbooks & Regex Scripts
at_seo_desc: Generate SillyTavern character personas, opening greetings, worldbook entries, regex scripts and polished text with AI — right in your browser. Bring your own API key (BYOK); nothing is uploaded.
at_tagline: Five AI generators for everything your tavern needs
at_desc: A suite of AI generators for SillyTavern players: character personas, opening greetings, worldbook entries, regex scripts and text polishing. Calls your own API straight from your browser (BYOK) — your key and your content never leave your device.
at_feature_1_desc: A name plus a one-line concept becomes a complete character: description, personality, scenario, first message, dialogue examples and tags — as JSON or YAML.
at_feature_2_desc: Produce 1-3 alternate openings for any card in your library (or a hand-written brief), in first or third person, ready to append with one click.
at_feature_3_desc: Describe a setting and get 3-10 structured lorebook entries with trigger keywords, titles and third-person content — staged in an editable table.
at_feature_4_desc: Describe a text transformation and receive a validated SillyTavern regex script: find pattern, replacement, placement and depth bounds included.
at_feature_5_desc: Trim tokens, improve readability, strip emojis or fix translationese — with an option to preserve formatting and macros.
at_feature_6_desc: Reuses the API settings from the web app: generation streams straight from your provider to your browser. No account, no server-side storage.
at_step_1_desc: Open Settings and enter your own API endpoint and key (or switch to the built-in local backend). The key stays in your browser.
at_step_2_desc: Pick a tab and fill in the short form — concept, scene, topic or purpose — then choose the output language and creativity.
at_step_3_title: Watch it stream, then keep it
at_step_3_desc: Results stream in live. Copy, download, append to a card, save as a worldbook — or send it straight into the web app and start playing.
at_ws_desc: Runs entirely in your browser and calls the API you configure. Generated content is saved only to your local library.
at_faq_q1: Do I need an API key?
at_faq_a1: Yes — the toolkit calls an AI model with your own credentials (BYOK). Open Settings to enter an endpoint and key, or switch the backend to the built-in WebLLM to run a local model.
at_faq_q2: Where does my key and content go?
at_faq_a2: Nowhere but your browser. Requests go straight from your browser to the provider you configured; generated cards, greetings and worldbooks are stored only in your local library.
at_faq_a3: Personas export as full SillyTavern V2 card JSON, greetings append to a card's alternate_greetings, worldbook entries become standard SillyTavern world info books, and regex scripts match the regex extension's format.
at_faq_q4: Can I edit what the AI wrote?
at_faq_a4: Of course. Greetings and persona fields are plain text you can copy anywhere, worldbook entries land in an editable staging table, and everything can be regenerated with a different creativity or language.

sw_seo_title: Story to Worldbook — Turn Novels into SillyTavern Worldbook Entries Online
sw_seo_desc: Split a long novel or document into chapters and distill each one into SillyTavern worldbook entries with AI: adjustable splitting, focus and detail controls, duplicate detection, one-click export. BYOK — everything runs in your browser.
sw_tagline: Turn long novels into ready-to-use SillyTavern worldbooks, chapter by chapter
sw_desc: Paste a long story or upload .txt/.md files: the tool splits it into chapters, then distills each chapter into world info entries — keywords, titles and third-person lore text — with your own AI key. Review everything in a staging table with duplicate detection, then save it to your library or export standard SillyTavern worldbook JSON. Nothing ever leaves your browser.
sw_feature_1_desc: Recognizes 第X章/回/卷, Chapter N, markdown headings and --- separators automatically. Every split point stays adjustable: rename, merge, exclude or re-split — nothing is locked in.
sw_feature_2_desc: Each chunk is sent to your own AI with a strict-JSON contract: trigger keywords, entry titles and self-contained third-person lore content, grounded in what the text actually says.
sw_feature_3_desc: Steer extraction toward characters, locations, events, world settings or items; choose entries per chunk, keyword language and one of three detail levels, plus free-form extra instructions.
sw_feature_4_desc: Every extracted entry lands in an editable staging table: fix titles, tweak keywords, rewrite content. Possible duplicates are flagged so you can merge them or keep both with one click.
sw_feature_5_desc: Entries are completed with all SillyTavern world info fields and sensible defaults. Save to the built-in library, download a .json that ST imports directly, or copy to clipboard.
sw_feature_6_desc: Uses your own API key (OpenAI-compatible endpoints or local WebLLM) stored only in your browser. Your novel text is processed locally and sent only to the AI endpoint you configure.
sw_step_1_desc: Drop a long novel into the textarea or upload .txt/.md files — multiple files are concatenated in order. Optionally pick a reference character card for context.
sw_step_2_desc: The text is split into chunks by chapter headings (or size). Rename, merge, exclude and preview every chunk until the boundaries feel right.
sw_step_3_desc: Set entries per chunk, focus, keyword language and detail, then run the batch. Edit staged entries, resolve duplicates and save or download your worldbook.
sw_ws_desc: A four-step wizard: input → split → settings → batch extraction. Data stays in your browser; AI calls use your own key.
sw_faq_a1: Any long prose: novels, fan fiction, setting bibles, campaign notes. Plain .txt/.md files or pasted text both work. Splitting recognizes Chinese chapter headings (第X章/节/回/卷), English “Chapter N”, markdown headings and --- separators; without any of those it falls back to ~2000-character blocks cut at paragraph boundaries.
sw_faq_q2: Which AI does it use and what does it cost?
sw_faq_a2: It is BYOK — bring your own key. Configure any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (or local WebLLM) in Settings; the key is stored only in your browser and requests go straight from your browser to that endpoint. The tool itself is free; your provider bills your usage as usual.
sw_faq_q3: How are keywords chosen, and what about duplicates?
sw_faq_a3: The AI is instructed to pick 1-3 short keywords that appear in the story text, in the keyword language you choose. Every keyword is editable afterwards. Entries with the same title or identical keywords are flagged as possible duplicates so you can merge or keep them.
sw_faq_a4: Everything — pasted text, chunks, staged entries and saved worldbooks — lives in your browser's local storage. Saving to the library keeps it in this browser; the downloaded .json can be imported into SillyTavern or shared anywhere.
